chapter: Opening and the early lawn-party bands
title: Bab Frank's ragtime lawn-party band
summary: Vincent recalls Bab Frank's band playing lawn parties when he was 11 to 14, with Henry Martin and Kutcher Martin, and says it was a ragtime band whose players mostly could not read.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: So he wanted to talk about Bab Frank. I'll tell you a message I know about him. I was young then, you know. He had Bab Frank. He had a good band in his days, you know. He had a 70th band. He used to play all for these lawn parties, they called him at that time, yeah. And, uh, he was good at that time. He played a piccolo. Yeah, Kutcher Martin with him. Henry Martin. And I just remember who else he had, you know. But yeah, he was strong. He and John Robeshoe were the strongest one at that time, you know. For pinnacle, I mean for lawn parties, you know. And he'd serve people packing jams. Them children could go there at that time, you know, around my age. 11, 12, 14 with the parents, you know. And he used to always draw crowds, you know. Ask him what kind of band was it.
Was it a ragtime band or a reading band?

He said, was it a ragtime band or a reading band? Well, he was, he was, he was, Frank and Reed, but I don't know about Henry and Kutcher. I don't think I could read. But he had a good band, you know. He was a good band, you know. In them days, you know. It was a jazz, a rag band, you know. Ragtime? Yeah, ragtime band.
